start_here: Say to your AI: "Check which files my kept-files list says I can get back and show me what could go to Trash, moving nothing", with {"rows": [{"id": "synthetic:empty-row", "value": {}}]}. It runs tool:free-what-the-list-says-can-be-got-back and answers which rows are eligible, with the path and generation each would hand to the native Trash step. It moves nothing.
no_lists_because: It keeps no list of its own: it reads the rows you pass from your own list of files and how to get them back.
instructions: 1. Read up to 100 rows of your list of files and how to get them back (each { id, value }).
2. Say "Show me what can go to Trash". The AI runs tool:free-what-the-list-says-can-be-got-back with those rows; nothing moves.

3. Read eligible_count, eligible_path_bytes and each row's reason. The native Trash step (the caller, inside the folder you granted) moves each eligible path to the recoverable Trash only while it still has its trash_handoff expected_generation, then writes that row's moved state. The tool moves nothing and writes no list.
